text:
alex_support: Customer (AcmeApps) opened a support ticket — sudden spike of 429s + p50 latency up to 700-1200ms for requests they believe are pinned to eu-west. They say this started ~2026-03-17 10:22 UTC.
alex_support: They included response headers showing `X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1` on some successful responses. Customer insists they didn't change routing. Need quick triage.
mira_infra: Can you paste a sample request/response (headers + trace id) and the org id? I'll check region metrics/queues.
alex_support: Org: org_acme_451. Sample curl + response snippet pasted below:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX" \\
  -H "X-Redwood-Api-Version: 2026-02-01" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"hello"}' \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1
< X-Redwood-Route: soft-fallback
< X-Request-Id: rwd-req-20260317-9b2f
```

alex_support: They also attached a trace where the SDK shows `route_decision=soft_fallback` and `fallback_reason=region_capacity`.

mira_infra: Pulling region metrics now for eu-west. Give me 2 min.

ops-bot: [AUTO ALERT] region-eu-west queue_depth > 1k (10:21:12 UTC), 429_rate 4.8% across short tail.

mira_infra: Confirmed: between 10:20-10:30 UTC eu-west accepted rate spiked, queue_depth peaked ~1.2k, available_worker_slots 380. Autoscaler didn't add capacity because `reserved_pool_mode=private_reserve` and reserved pool is exhausted for that org.

sam_runtime: Autoscaler log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T10:19:55Z] scale_decision: need +6 instances
[2026-03-17T10:20:02Z] plan_apply: aborted -> billing_hold_or_reserved_depleted
```

mira_infra: Also seeing that the fallback policy for this customer's route is `soft-fallback:allow` (system-level). That means when eu-west is congested we route to nearest compatible region (us-east) instead of rejecting. That matches the `X-Redwood-Route: soft-fallback` header.

jen_prod: Any chance a recent routing change made eu-west treat this org as non-priority? I saw a PR touching priority classes yesterday.

mira_infra: Checked policy matrix: org_acme_451 is on standard tier (no SLA override). Yesterday's policy PR changed how reserved pools are counted for enterprise vs standard; this org falls into the affected path -> its reserved capacity didn't auto-burst beyond its pool.

alex_support: Customer is also worried about billing — they saw a "billing paused" banner in console earlier today. Could that explain autoscaler abort?

mira_infra: Yes. The autoscaler refused to spin up more *paid* dedicated workers because account flagged for expired invoice. The reserved_pool still has in-use capacity but no burst allowed when billing_hold=true.

sam_runtime: So two-fold root cause: (1) org consumed reserved capacity in eu-west, (2) billing hold prevented autoscaler from acquiring burst capacity -> region saturated -> soft-fallback routed traffic to us-east.

alex_support: Repro steps I gave the customer to surface routing: 1) make a request with their org key 2) check `X-Redwood-Route` and `X-Redwood-Region` headers 3) use `--trace` in SDK to see `fallback_reason` field. They confirmed consistent behavior.

mira_infra: Short-term mitigation options:
- remove `soft-fallback:allow` on org route (force reject instead of cross-region detour) -> reduces unexpected cross-region latency but increases 429s.
- manually buy/allocate a one-off burst capacity to eu-west for this org (requires billing cleared + ops approval).
- ask customer to temporarily set `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` header from client (sticky pin) to force local region; will fail if queue saturates.

jen_prod: Also propose we surface `billing_hold` status in routing logs and in the console routing page. Right now it's subtle.

alex_support: Customer asked for a quick test. I asked them to clear outstanding invoice and confirm. They cleared a $1k invoice at 10:40 UTC and let us know.

ops-bot: [AUTO INFO] billing.status changed -> ok for org_acme_451 (10:41:07 UTC)

mira_infra: After billing cleared, autoscaler applied a recovery plan: +8 instances to eu-west at 10:42:30. Queue depth backfilled over ~3 minutes. Observed `X-Redwood-Route` went from `soft-fallback` -> `primary` for new requests.

alex_support: Customer reran their load test at 10:46 and reports p50 dropped to ~95ms and 429s disappeared.

sam_runtime: Root cause summary (for postmortem): reserved_pool_exhaustion + billing_hold preventing burst scaling -> region saturation -> system-level soft-fallback routing enabled cross-region detours (us-east) causing latency spikes for pinned customers. Secondary contributing factor: config change last PR tightened burst rules for standard-tier orgs.

jen_prod: Action items:
- [mira_infra] add log line to route decision when billing_hold prevents scaling (priority: high)
- [sam_runtime] revert/adjust PR that tightened burst rules for standard tier (priority: medium)
- [product] add UI telemetry for org billing status in routing page (priority: medium)
- [alex_support] confirm closure with customer and share postmortem

alex_support: I'll draft an incident summary for the customer and include repro steps + mitigation (billing clear or request region-pin header until we change policy). I'll update here when sent.

alex_support: Sent summary to customer at 11:05 UTC. They replied: "Thanks — cleared invoice, seems good now. Please notify if this reoccurs." :thumbsup:

mira_infra: I'll follow up with a small telemetry dashboard to show when fallback=soft-fallback is used per org.

alex_support: Marking thread resolved after customer confirmation. If anyone wants to add more notes for the postmortem, append here.

sam_runtime: adding note about adding a rate-limiter override for pinned orgs so they either get reject (fast) or protected burst.

jen_prod: Filing a short postmortem doc and linking to this thread.

alex_support: closing — resolved.
